incidents-bot: Pager: HIGH - gpu-queue-latency > 120s in us-west-2 (detected 2332109875)
incidents-bot: Severity: P1, Impact: some customers experiencing long inference queue times, autoscaler attempted 3 times and hit scale limit.
Mia Chen: I'm on it. seeing queue growth on scheduler A and B, CPU looks fine but GPU allocation failing.
Mia Chen: top of stack: autoscaler logs show repeated "scale request rejected: capacity fragment, no matching MIG slice"
Raj Patel: paste of recent autoscaler snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:17:02Z autoscaler: scale_request: delta=+24 gpus
2026-03-15T14:17:02Z allocator: found candidate nodes=0; reason=fragmented_mig_slots
2026-03-15T14:17:03Z autoscaler: retrying scale but reached cap=20 active_nodes
```
Raj Patel: We're at the cluster reserved max (20). autoscaler cannot add a new node pool because quota is hit.
Henry Wu: Scheduler logs (recent):
```
[EPOCH] allocation failed: request=(1xA100-80GB-MIG-1g.16gb), available_slices=[{migsizes:[1,2,4]}, {migsizes:[2,4]}]
match_score: 0.0 -> placement rejected due to mismatch
```
Henry Wu: Short version: MIG sizing mismatch + binpacking means many free GPU memory/SMs are stranded across nodes but not in the right slice sizes for incoming jobs.
Jordana Park: Customer impact? who is affected?
Emily S: CS pulled live: TenantAlpha (prod real-time), TenantBeta (batch inference), internal eval jobs. TenantAlpha is reporting 500ms -> 5s enqueuing, visible errors in their SDK for timeouts.
Carlos Morales: I've notified account exec for TenantAlpha, escalated.
Mia Chen: Immediate mitigations suggestion list:
1) Pause autoscaler policy that tries to create more of same node type (prevents flapping).
2) Trigger manual scale: spin up 2 x different-config nodes that provide matching MIG slice shapes (workaround).
3) Evict low-priority long-running eval pods to free compatible MIG slices.
4) Fallback: route high-priority customers to smaller quantized model running on CPU/GPU pooled nodes.
Raj Patel: I'm going to pause autoscaler. running: `kubectl annotate cm autoscaler-config pause=true --overwrite`
Raj Patel: paused. autoscaler log now: "manual pause set by Raj Patel at 2332109930"
Mia Chen: Good. Henry can you list nodes with available MIG slots and shapes?
Henry Wu: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.allocatable.gpuslice}\n'` output summarised:
- node-gpu-05: slices=[1g,1g,2g] free=1
- node-gpu-09: slices=[4g] free=0
- node-gpu-11: slices=[2g,2g] free=2 (but already reserved)
Henry Wu: There's enough aggregate GPU but shapes don't match 16gb job.
Jordana Park: What's the plan for TenantAlpha meantime? SLA?
Emily S: We offered a degraded fallback: 90% of requests route to a condensed model with slightly lower accuracy (opt-in). TenantAlpha accepted temporary fallback for 15 minutes.
Carlos Morales: Noted. Informed customer success: they're monitoring.
Mia Chen: I'm going to manually provision 2 nodes with 1xA100-80gb (no MIG) to accept current queued jobs. Command: `gcloud compute instances create rwd-temp-gpu-1 --machine-type a2-highgpu-1g --zone us-west2-a` (running now).
Mia Chen: temp nodes are provisioning (2332110050).
Raj Patel: While those boot, I'll attempt live compaction: drain a low-priority node and recreate pods with smaller MIG requests to better pack. This is risky but should free contiguous slots.
Henry Wu: Starting drains on node-gpu-08 (low priority) at 2332110100. running: `kubectl drain node-gpu-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
Mia Chen: New temp nodes came up and registered as workers (2332110245). scheduler now able to place ~6 queued jobs on temp nodes. queue length dropping.
Emily S: TenantAlpha latencies improving to 350ms enqueue. CS reporting reduced errors.
Jordana Park: Good. any ongoing root cause notes?
Raj Patel: Initial hypothesis: during a previous resize we migrated workloads to smaller MIG partitions to fit more low-latency jobs; later a surge of large 16GB jobs created a mismatch. autoscaler hit cluster reserved cap (20) due to conservative quotas, and binpacking logic didn't have fallback to consolidate MIG slices.
Carlos Morales: Are there any control-plane alerts to change?
Mia Chen: Action items (immediate):
- [Mia] keep temp nodes for next 30m then rollback if stable.
- [Raj] update autoscaler policy to allow temporary burst up to 24 nodes for emergency (need approvals).
- [Henry] run background recombine job to prefer co-locating similar MIG sizes when scheduling low-priority pods.
- [Jordana] coordinate customer comms and follow up with TenantAlpha.
- [Emily] capture error-level logs and timers for postmortem.
cs-bot: Noted: Incident logged INC-2026-1423, severity P1, workaround applied: routing fallback + manual temp nodes.
Mia Chen: Handoff to next on-call in 30m. Leaving this thread open for updates.
Raj Patel: filing a postmortem stub, assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml. ticket: PM-INC-2332109876 (will link here).
Henry Wu: I'll start a short-term scheduler tweak: prefer packing by MIG profile at pod admission. Testing in staging first.
Jordana Park: Thanks team. I'll send a short update to the incident channel and CS.
Mia Chen: Final status (2332110450): Queues reduced to normal, TenantAlpha on fallback for 10 more minutes then migrate back. Marking as mitigated; creating followup tasks for long-term fix (autoscaler burst allowances, MIG compaction algorithm).
incidents-bot: Incident P1 mitigated by operator action. Please attach timeline + logs to INC-2026-1423 for postmortem.
